title: GPT Web App Generator - 10,000 apps created in a month: Matija Sosic
talk_summary: A GPT-powered full-stack app generator (Mage) that produced 10,000 apps in a month by constraining generation to one framework (Wasp/React/Node), pre-generating boilerplate without LLM calls, and splitting work across model tiers. It reports 10-20 cents per app by using GPT-4 only for planning and GPT-3.5 for implementation, plus heuristic error-fixing that resolved ~90% of common errors.

takeaways.technique: Tiered model assignment by pipeline stage
takeaways.what_they_do: Use the expensive/strong model only for the planning stage (most creative, complex) and a cheaper/faster model for implementation, since the framework constrains the output space.
takeaways.numbers: 10-20 cents/app vs $1-2/app if GPT-4 used everywhere (10x cost reduction)

takeaways.technique: Step Zero: pre-generate deterministic scaffolding without LLM
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the target stack is fixed, they emit config files, auth logic, and global CSS from templates before calling the model at all.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can produce a lot of code up front without even touching the open AI API and asking GPT any questions

takeaways.technique: Heuristic auto-fix for known recurring errors
takeaways.what_they_do: They catalogued the most common model mistakes (e.g., default vs named imports) and fixed many with simple heuristics without invoking the LLM; this handled most errors.
takeaways.numbers: ~90% of all errors handled by heuristics

takeaways.technique: Constrain the problem domain to shrink error space
takeaways.what_they_do: Specializing to one stack (React/Node/Wasp) let them assume structure up front, removing boilerplate and reducing the space for model errors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it is specialized only for full stack web apps and nothing else ... that allows us to assume a lot up front

takeaways.technique: Explicit plan → generate → self-fix loop with bounded retries
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent runs three phases: plan (entities, queries, pages), implement, then detect-and-fix errors, retrying until no detectable errors remain.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the code agent work consists of three main phases planning generating the code and fixing the errors
takeaways.numbers: ~27,000 tokens for a full app generation

takeaways.technique: Track per-stage token cost and error taxonomy
takeaways.what_they_do: They instrumented generation logs to see phase-by-phase token spend and catalogued the model's most common error types to drive fixes.
